record.paper_title: Minimal positive realizations: a survey of recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For a transfer function that admits a positive realization, what are the best possible lower and upper bounds on the minimal order of a positive realization? In particular, can one derive tight bounds that depend explicitly on the system data and that sharply bracket the smallest achievable positive state dimension?

evidence.quote: - find "tight" lower and upper bounds to minimal order of a positive realization 1.
1Some interesting preliminary results can be found in reference [14].

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let H(z) be a rational transfer function (with real coefficients) that admits a positive realization, i.e., there exist a nonnegative integer n and matrices A ∈ ℝ^{n×n}, b ∈ ℝ^{n×1}, c ∈ ℝ^{1×n}, d ∈ ℝ with all entries nonnegative, such that H(z) = d + c(zI − A)^{-1} b. Define the minimal positive realization order n_+(H) as the smallest such n. Determine the best possible lower and upper bounds on n_+(H): namely, find computable functions L(H) and U(H), depending explicitly on the system data of H (for example its poles, zeros, impulse-response coefficients, McMillan degree, etc.), such that L(H) ≤ n_+(H) ≤ U(H), and such that these bounds are tight in the sense that for every admissible H both bounds can be attained (or approached) by some transfer function with the given data. In particular, can one give matching lower and upper bounds that sharply bracket n_+(H) for all positively realizable H?
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of determining the minimal dimension of a positive realization remains open. Only lower and upper bounds are known, with tight (matching) results available only in special cases (e.g., third-order transfer functions with distinct real poles, transfer functions with positive real or nonnegative multiple poles, and minimal positive Markov realizations). Recent works (2020s) continue to refine upper bounds but do not provide tight bounds in the general setting.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive realizations: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Only lower and upper bounds for the dimension of a minimal positive realization have been given to date.
status_evidence.claim: General tight bounds on minimal positive realization order are not known; only non-matching lower/upper bounds exist.

status_evidence.title: An upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations for discrete time systems
status_evidence.snippet: Provides an upper bound on the dimension of minimal positive realizations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research continues to derive new upper bounds, indicating the gap between known lower and upper bounds is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Minimal positive Markov realizations
status_evidence.snippet: Linear programming approach for minimum dimension positive Markov realizations, which serves as an upper bound on minimal positive realization dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Computable upper bounds are obtained via positive Markov realizations, but the general minimal positive realization order is still bracketed, not determined exactly.
